name: Large sets with divisibility-incomparable subset sums
description: construct() -> 1..30 distinct integers in 1..256. Form every NONEMPTY subset sum; no two distinct resulting values may divide one another. Equal sum values are deduplicated (but any repeated subset representation also leads to a forbidden double after cancellation). Maximize set size. The local N=256 construction is checked by exact reachability and a multiples sieve. The empty sum is excluded, and no general asymptotic improvement or formal proof is claimed.

sources.locator: Konstantinos Gaitanas, Two divisibility problems on subset sums (2019). Section 4, Problem two, defines property R: subset sums form a multiple-free sequence, and attributes the original extremal question to Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor and Sárközy (1999).

Paul Erdős, Vsevolod Lev, Gérard Rauzy, Csaba Sándor and András Sárközy, Greedy algorithm, arithmetic progressions, subset sums and divisibility (1999).
